name: White Fibrous Papulosis of the Neck

criteria.description: Presence of multiple small, white to skin-colored, firm papules localized predominantly on the lateral and posterior neck
Histological examination showing thickened, homogenized collagen bundles in the papillary dermis with minimal inflammation
Exclusion of other papular dermatoses such as pseudoxanthoma elasticum and elastosis perforans serpiginosa
Onset typically in middle-aged to elderly adults

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of characteristic clinical presentation and confirmatory histopathology with exclusion of other similar dermatoses
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by histopathology; genetic testing is not established.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Multiple white to skin-colored firm papules on the neck
pathognomonic.notes: Localized mainly on lateral and posterior neck
searchTerms: multiple firm white bumps on neck

pathognomonic.symptomName: Thickened fibrous collagen bundles in papillary dermis
searchTerms: thickened collagen in upper skin layer

common.notes: Typically no associated pruritus or pain

common.symptomName: Slow progression of papules over years
common.notes: Gradual increase in number and size

common.symptomName: Predominant involvement of middle-aged to elderly adults
searchTerms: mostly affects middle-aged and older adults
evenly spread skin lesions on both sides

occasional.symptomName: Mild skin roughness or textural changes
Presence of similar papules on upper back or shoulders
searchTerms: similar bumps on upper back or shoulders
lesions on back and shoulder skin

rare.symptomName: Papules on other body sites such as forearms
searchTerms: papules on forearms or other sites
mild skin wasting associated with bumps

other: Histopathology showing thickened, homogenized collagen bundles in papillary dermis
Absence of elastic fiber fragmentation or calcification

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of yellowish papules with elastic fiber fragmentation
Systemic involvement including cardiovascular and ophthalmological manifestations
Histology shows calcified and fragmented elastic fibers
Papules with transepidermal elimination of elastic fibers

redFlags: Presence of systemic symptoms such as vision changes or cardiovascular abnormalities
Signs of secondary infection or ulceration of lesions
